findings.title: Local cache entry is set before the store call, so a rejected device bypasses the limit on its next request
findings.body: `tagDeviceUI` calls `localCache.SetDefault(key, ...)` before `CreateOrUpdateDevice`. When the store returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, the cache key is already set. The first request from that device is rejected. Every later request within the cache TTL (29 minutes) hits `localCache.Get(key)`, returns nil and is authenticated as anonymous without being recorded. The limit is therefore only enforced once per device per TTL, so any over-limit device gets through on retry or page reload. The same ordering also means a transient DB error suppresses retries for 29 minutes. Fix: set the cache entry only after `CreateOrUpdateDevice` succeeds, or delete it on error.

findings.title: Check-then-insert on the device limit is racy and can exceed the configured limit
findings.body: `CreateOrUpdateDevice` runs `CountDevices` in one session and then does the `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT` in a separate session, with no transaction or lock. N concurrent requests from N new devices can all read `count < deviceLimit` and all insert, so the table can overshoot the limit, and more so with several Grafana instances. Fix: do the count and insert atomically, for example `INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) ...) < limit`, or use a serialized transaction. At minimum, document the limit as approximate.

findings.title: Device tagging moved from a background goroutine into the authentication path
findings.body: `TagDevice` used to run in a goroutine with its own 2-minute timeout and panic recovery. It now runs synchronously on the request context. Every anonymous request from an uncached device now waits for DB work: a `COUNT(*)` when a limit is set, plus a write. A slow or locked DB therefore slows or fails anonymous requests. Request cancellation also aborts the tagging write. The panic recovery that guarded this code is gone as well. Only the limit-reached error needs to be synchronous. Consider keeping the non-limit path async, or at least a bounded timeout.

findings.title: Device limit behavior is only minimally tested
findings.body: Only one test covers the limit: a new device is rejected once the limit is reached. Nothing tests that an existing device within the 30-day window can still be updated at the limit, or that a device older than 30 days is rejected. Nothing covers the `Anonymous.Authenticate` change that now returns an error on `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. Nothing covers the local-cache interaction, which is where the real bug in this change sits. A test for repeated requests from a rejected device would have caught it.

findings.title: New `device_limit` option is undocumented
findings.body: The new `[auth.anonymous] device_limit` setting is read here, but it is not added to `conf/defaults.ini`, `conf/sample.ini` or the docs. The PR description is also an empty template. It is not documented that 0 (or any non-positive value) means unlimited, that the limit counts devices seen in the last 30 days, or that over-limit new devices are rejected with an authentication error. Operators cannot discover or safely use the setting.
